title: Commitment Hedge + Preemptible Overlay experiment for Dedicated capacity packaging
creator: Connor Liu
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers want lower unit costs for sustained inference while maintaining contractual uptime guarantees. Pure reserved capacity is expensive for bursty, uneven workloads; on-demand is costly. We need a packaging experiment that offers predictable base capacity pricing plus an economically attractive overlay for lower-priority capacity (preemptible) with contractual crediting to preserve SLA trust.

This ticket proposes a new commercial construct "Commitment Hedge + Preemptible Overlay" that blends: (1) base reserved commitment (sustained), (2) preemptible overlay pool at a steep discount, and (3) a credit system that compensates customers for preemptions or capacity shortfalls that materially affect throughput/SLOs.
hypothesis: If we offer a hedged commitment product (base reserved + preemptible overlay with transparent preemption crediting), then enterprise customers with variable workloads will accept higher committed volumes and longer terms, increasing committed revenue by >=15% while keeping average unit price lower and SLA complaints unchanged.
experiment_design:
1) Offer a three-tier sample offer to 10 pilot accounts:
   - Tier A (Conservative): 70% base commit, 20% preemptible overlay, 10% on-demand; smaller credit multiplier.
   - Tier B (Balanced): 50% base, 40% preemptible, 10% on-demand; medium credit multiplier.
   - Tier C (Aggressive): 30% base, 60% preemptible, 10% on-demand; high preemption credits.

2) Pricing: base = list-price * commit-discount; preemptible = base * 0.35-0.55 discount; credits accrue when preemption leads to >x% throughput degradation vs baseline.

3) Contract mechanics: define preemption windows, credit calculation, measurement signals (token throughput p99, queue time, canary synthetic tests).

4) Duration: 6-week pilot per account; telemetry and invoices instrumented to show credits.

5) Operators: Sales + Solutions + Customer Success run offers; Eng provides telemetry hook and preemption logging; Legal drafts SOW/Amendment.
pricing_matrix:
Example pricing bands (illustrative):
  - Base reserved capacity: 1.0x unit price * committed discount (15-25% depending on term).
  - Preemptible overlay: 0.45x - 0.65x base after commit discount (sliding by preemption SLA).
  - Burst on-demand: standard on-demand price (no discount).
  - Preemption credit: when preemption causes >5% loss of expected throughput for a 15-minute window, credit = min(issued_credits, 5% of committed-monthly fee) * credit_multiplier (1.0-2.5 depending on tier).

We will publish an explicit per-GPU-hour equivalent and sample invoice rows for transparency.
contract_changes:
Proposed SOW amendment language highlights:
  - "Preemptible overlay" defined as lower-priority instances which may be interrupted with X-minute warning.
  - Observable SLOs remain tied to committed capacity; credits apply when measured delivery falls below the SLO due to preemption or capacity shortfall.
  - Credit caps: monthly cap at Y% of committed fees.
  - Term and early-termination: early termination triggers a true-up on committed vs consumed.
  - Auditability: customer has access to preemption logs + synthetic test results.
  - Data residency and isolation: preemptible workload runs on same HW but logical isolation maintained; no cross-tenant data sharing.

Legal to review: indemnity changes around preemption, updated SLA language, definition of force majeure related to regional capacity outages.
security_qna_notes:
Security and compliance items to include in the updated enterprise questionnaire for pilot customers:
  - Confirm KMS/HSM integration for keys used in private deployments.
  - Confirm encryption at rest and in transit for data persisted during overlay preemptions.
  - Audit logs: preemption events, actor IDs, timestamps exported to customer SIEM if requested (S3/CloudStorage).
  - RBAC controls for staff to access preemptible pools and telemetry.
  - SOC2 / ISO attestation references and any required third-party attestation for on-prem or VPC variants.
  - Backup/restore guarantees for cached KV state when tasks are preempted.

Security ask: short questionnaire response (1-2 pages) and a tick-box for additional HSM onboarding.
metrics: Preemption rate (percent of overlay capacity preempted per week)
Credits issued (USD) and percent of monthly invoice
Churn risk flags and early termination requests
acceptance_criteria: >=15% uplift in committed revenue from pilot accounts or justified pipeline expansion by sales
Average unit cost to customer <= 90% of existing reserved-only scenario for equivalent throughput
Preemption credits remain <= 8% of committed monthly fees across pilot accounts
No material SLO regressions on committed capacity (p99 latency increase <=5%)
Legal and Security sign-off for template amendment and QnA responses
rollout_plan: Week 0-2: finalize pricing bands, legal amendment template, security QnA template, instrument telemetry; choose 10 pilot customers.
Week 3-8: run pilot, weekly sync between Sales/CS/Eng/Product; log incidents and crediting events.
Week 9: analyze pilot data, calculate economics, update playbook and sample contract language.
Week 10-12: prepare GA packaging if acceptance criteria met, update Console to surface preemptible overlay usage and credits on invoices.
risks: Customers misunderstand preemption semantics leading to support load
Engineering changes required to expose deterministic preemption logs/metrics delay experiment start
Credits could materially erode margin if preemption rate spikes during regional outages
Legal pushback on auditability or indemnity language
Security concerns for shared hardware in sensitive workloads may reduce adoption
